Enforces this at runtime to catch bugs where the wrong accessor is used, and fixes an inconsistent -blockfilterindex parsing bug along the way

result.summary: This PR adds ALLOW_LIST as a real flag on ArgsManager arguments and enforces, via CheckArgFlags, that GetArg()/IsArgSet() are never called on list-type arguments and GetArgs() is never called on non-list arguments. It also fixes a long-standing inconsistency where -blockfilterindex="" sometimes enabled all indexes and sometimes triggered an error depending on argument order. The bulk of the diff is a scripted-diff tagging existing list arguments plus corresponding test and fuzz-harness updates.
result.problem: ArgsManager's GetArg/GetArgs/IsArgSet methods are easy to misuse on list-valued settings (returning only the last or first value, or misreporting emptiness), a footgun for anyone adding or maintaining command-line/config options across the codebase.

open_concerns: ajtowns wondered whether these checks should eventually be compile-time rather than runtime; acknowledged as a possible future improvement, not blocking
ryanofsky noted IsArgSet is 'generally broken and misused for list settings', pointed at follow-up PR #17783 to address more broadly

result.card: This PR gives ArgsManager a real ALLOW_LIST flag and enforces, via CheckArgFlags, that list-valued settings are always read with GetArgs() and non-list settings with GetArg()/IsArgSet(), closing a footgun that has caused at least one real bug (inconsistent -blockfilterindex="" parsing, now fixed to behave consistently). It is a foundational refactor for two other open PRs, #17493 and #17783, which build directly on the flags introduced here. Concept ACKs came in early from hebasto, promag, and ajtowns with no unresolved objections, but the PR is a draft stacked on another draft, #16545, and a maintainer (fanquake) explicitly cited that as the reason to pause review; there has been no substantive reviewer engagement since 2020 despite the author rebasing it roughly 35 times over six years to keep it mergeable. Its priority rests on preventing a class of latent argument-handling bugs across the whole option surface rather than on any single dramatic fix.
